For example, filtering tasks by status=in_progress or triage by tag=cli is lost on reload. Filter state should be persisted in URL query parameters so that refreshing preserves the view, and URLs are shareable/bookmarkable.\n\n**Where**: The tasks page (`packages/web-ui/src/routes/tasks/+page.svelte`) already partially implements URL-based filters — it reads from `$page.url.searchParams` (line 39-47) via the `filterParams` derived value. However, the triage page (`packages/web-ui/src/routes/triage/+page.svelte`) uses local `$state` variables (`filterTag`, `filterStatus` at lines 43-44) that are NOT synced to URL params. Other list pages (items, inbox) likely have the same issue.\n\nKey files to update:\n- `packages/web-ui/src/routes/triage/+page.svelte` — filterTag and filterStatus need URL param sync\n- `packages/web-ui/src/routes/items/+page.svelte` — check if filters use URL params\n- Any other list/filter pages under `packages/web-ui/src/routes/`\n\n**How**: Follow the pattern already established in the tasks page:\n1. Read initial filter values from `$page.url.searchParams` (from `$app/stores`)\n2. When a filter changes, use `goto()` (from `$app/navigation`) to update URL params without a full page reload: `goto(\\`?status=\\${filterStatus}&tag=\\${filterTag}\\`, { replaceState: true, keepFocus: true })`\n3. Use `$derived` to compute filter values from URL params (like tasks page does)\n4. This approach gives: URL persistence, back/forward navigation, shareable links\n\nFor the triage page specifically:\n- Replace `let filterTag = $state('')` with reading from `$page.url.searchParams.get('tag')`\n- Replace `let filterStatus = $state('all')` with reading from `$page.url.searchParams.get('status')`\n- Add `goto()` calls when filters change\n\n**Done when**:\n- All list/filter pages read initial state from URL query params\n- Changing a filter updates the URL without full page reload\n- Refreshing the page preserves filter state\n- Browser back/forward navigates between filter states\n- The triage page URL shows filters like `?status=untriaged&tag=cli`",

## Specs

```yaml
- title: Stale Active Session Cleanup
  slug: session-stale-cleanup
  type: feature
  parent: "@session-events"
  description: |
    Detect and close stale active sessions so maintenance commands like
    session compaction can proceed without manual cleanup. The cleanup path
    must be safe, auditable, and previewable before mutation.
  traits:
    - trait-json-output
    - trait-dry-run
    - trait-semantic-exit-codes
    - trait-shadow-commit
    - trait-error-guidance
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        one or more sessions are currently in status "active"
      when: |
        user runs "kspec session stale close --dry-run"
      then: |
        command reports which sessions would be marked abandoned and includes
        per-session reasons without modifying any session files
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        stale active sessions match the configured criteria
      when: |
        user runs "kspec session stale close"
      then: |
        command marks only matching sessions abandoned and leaves all other
        session statuses unchanged
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        no active sessions match the stale criteria
      when: |
        command executes
      then: |
        command exits successfully and reports zero sessions changed
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        command runs in --all mode against many sessions
      when: |
        execution completes
      then: |
        output includes totals for candidates, changed sessions, skipped
        sessions, and failures in both human and JSON modes

- title: Stale Session Candidate Criteria
  slug: session-stale-criteria
  type: requirement
  parent: "@session-stale-cleanup"
  description: |
    Candidate selection is deterministic and based on explicit time criteria,
    not guessed session age.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        an active session has a most-recent event timestamp older than the
        inactivity threshold
      when: |
        stale candidates are computed
      then: |
        the session is eligible for closure if it also satisfies the age
        threshold
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        an active session has no events in events.jsonl
      when: |
        stale candidates are computed
      then: |
        started_at is used as the last-activity fallback timestamp
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        user provides both --older-than and --inactive-for criteria
      when: |
        candidates are filtered
      then: |
        both criteria are applied with AND logic
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        user provides an invalid time specification
      when: |
        command validates input
      then: |
        command returns usage error with guidance on accepted formats

- title: Auto-abandon Metadata and Audit Trail
  slug: session-stale-close-metadata
  type: requirement
  parent: "@session-stale-cleanup"
  description: |
    Automatic closure must preserve auditability so operators can understand
    why and when a session was auto-abandoned.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        a stale active session is selected for closure
      when: |
        closure is applied
      then: |
        session metadata is updated to status "abandoned" and ended_at is set
        to an ISO 8601 timestamp
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        a stale active session is auto-closed
      when: |
        close metadata is written
      then: |
        close_reason includes an "auto-abandoned" marker and the criteria
        used for selection
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        multiple sessions are auto-closed in one command
      when: |
        persistence completes
      then: |
        all metadata updates are captured in one shadow commit with a
        command-specific commit message
```

OK Started task: 01KJGBWNF

--- Spec Context ---
Implementing: Stale Active Session Cleanup

Detect and close stale active sessions so maintenance commands like
session compaction can proceed without manual cleanup. The cleanup path
must be safe, auditable, and previewable before mutation.


Acceptance Criteria (9):
  [ac-1]
    Given: one or more sessions are currently in status "active"

    When: user runs 'kspec session stale close --all --dry-run'
    Then: command reports which sessions would be marked abandoned and includes
per-session reasons without modifying any session files

        "created_at": "2026-02-26T19:38:54.292Z",
        "author": "@claude",
        "content": "ENRICHMENT — Standalone context for this task:\n\n**What**: The Web UI WebSocket connection continually disconnects and reconnects. The `WebSocketManager` in `packages/web-ui/src/lib/websocket/manager.ts` has exponential backoff reconnection (1s, 2s, 4s... max 30s, max 10 attempts), but users report seeing frequent disconnect/reconnect cycles in the console logs. This suggests either the server is closing connections, the keepalive/heartbeat mechanism is missing, or reconnection resets are happening incorrectly.\n\n**Where**:\n- `packages/web-ui/src/lib/websocket/manager.ts` — The WebSocketManager class. Key areas:\n  - `connect()` (line 150): creates WebSocket, sets up onopen/onmessage/onerror/onclose handlers\n  - `scheduleReconnect()` (line 371): exponential backoff logic, max 10 attempts\n  - `onclose` handler (line 183): triggers reconnect on any close event, even clean ones\n  - No heartbeat/ping mechanism — if the server expects periodic pings, the connection may time out\n- `packages/web-ui/src/lib/stores/connection.svelte.ts` — Connection store wrapping the manager\n- Server-side WebSocket handler (in the daemon code) — check if it sends pings or has idle timeouts\n\n**How**: Investigation and fix areas:\n1. **Add heartbeat/ping**: Implement a periodic ping from client to server (e.g., every 30s). Many WebSocket servers close idle connections after a timeout (often 60s). The client should send a ping command and expect a pong response.\n2. **Don't reconnect on clean close**: The `onclose` handler (line 183) calls `scheduleReconnect()` unconditionally. If `event.code === 1000` (normal closure) and the client initiated it via `disconnect()`, skip reconnection. Currently `disconnect()` clears the timer, but there's a race if onclose fires after disconnect resets state.\n3. **Check server-side idle timeout**: The daemon's WebSocket server may have an idle timeout that closes connections. Either increase it or implement heartbeat to keep alive.\n4. **Consider connection health check**: After reconnecting, verify the connection is actually healthy (e.g., send a ping and wait for response) before transitioning to 'connected' state.\n5. **Investigate MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS**: After 10 failed reconnects, the connection is abandoned permanently. Consider resetting the attempt counter after a successful connection that lasts longer than some threshold (e.g., 60s).\n\n**Done when**:\n- WebSocket connection remains stable for extended periods without spurious disconnects\n- Client sends periodic heartbeat/ping to prevent idle timeout\n- Clean disconnects (code 1000 from client-initiated disconnect) don't trigger reconnection\n- Console shows clean connection lifecycle without repeated disconnect/reconnect spam\n- Connection lost indicator (10s threshold) only triggers for genuine server unavailability\n- Tests cover: heartbeat keeps connection alive, clean close doesn't reconnect, reconnection works after genuine server restart",
        "supersedes": null
      },
      {
        "_ulid": "01KJDQX0Y1T915X3M23D1VS9PP",
        "created_at": "2026-02-26T19:48:05.698Z",
        "author": "@claude",
        "content": "Linked to @daemon-server spec (covers WebSocket protocol). Investigate and fix WebSocket reconnection reliability.",
        "supersedes": null
      }
    ],
    "todos": [],

]

    Then: Elysia HTTP server starts on configurable port (default 3456) binding to localhost only
  [ac-2]
    Given: daemon is starting
    When: server binds to network interface
    Then: only accepts connections from 127.0.0.1 and ::1 (IPv6 localhost)
  [ac-3]
    Given: connection attempt from non-localhost IP
    When: request received
    Then: connection rejected with 403 Forbidden
  [ac-4]
    Given: daemon is running
    When: any .kspec/*.yaml file changes
    Then: connected WebSocket clients receive update event via topic subscription
  [ac-5]
    Given: file watching is active
    When: rapid changes occur (< 500ms apart)
    Then: events are debounced and aggregated into single notification
  [ac-6]
    Given: watched file has YAML parse error
    When: change detected
    Then: error logged and WebSocket broadcasts error event (daemon does not crash)
  [ac-7]
    Given: .kspec directory becomes inaccessible
    When: watcher encounters error
    Then: daemon logs error and attempts recovery with exponential backoff
  [ac-8]
    Given: Bun fs.watch fails or misses events
    When: reliability issue detected
    Then: automatically fall back to Chokidar file watcher
  [ac-9]
    Given: daemon is running
    When: user runs 'kspec serve --daemon'
    Then: process detaches to background, writes PID to .kspec/.daemon.pid, CLI returns immediately
  [ac-10]
    Given: daemon is running in background
    When: user runs 'kspec serve stop'
    Then: daemon shuts down gracefully, removes PID file, closes all WebSocket connections
  [ac-11]
    Given: daemon is running
    When: GET /api/health is called
    Then: returns {status, uptime, connections, version} JSON
  [ac-12]
    Given: daemon receives SIGTERM or SIGINT
    When: shutdown signal received
    Then: graceful shutdown (flush pending messages, close connections, save state)
  [ac-13]
    Given: WebSocket connection established
    When: 30 seconds pass without activity
    Then: server sends ping frame
  [ac-14]
    Given: ping was sent
    When: no pong received within 90 seconds
    Then: connection closed with code 1001
  [ac-15]
    Given: Elysia server is configured
    When: routes are registered
    Then: use plugin pattern for middleware (CORS, logging, validation)
  [ac-16]
    Given: daemon code is ready
    When: bun build --compile runs
    Then: produces standalone executable without requiring Bun installation
  [ac-17]
    Given: daemon is running with web UI built
    When: browser opens http://localhost:<port>/
    Then: serves the built web UI assets (SvelteKit static build) as the root route

--- Spec Context ---
Implementing: Daemon Server Mode

Long-running Elysia.js server on Bun runtime that exposes kspec state via HTTP API and WebSocket
for real-time updates. Binds to localhost only for security. Supports foreground and background
modes with PID file management. Includes heartbeat ping/pong for connection health monitoring.


Acceptance Criteria (17):
  [ac-1]
    Given: kspec is installed
    When: user runs 'kspec serve'
    Then: Elysia HTTP server starts on configurable port (default 3456) binding to localhost only
  [ac-2]
    Given: daemon is starting
    When: server binds to network interface
    Then: only accepts connections from 127.0.0.1 and ::1 (IPv6 localhost)
  [ac-3]
    Given: connection attempt from non-localhost IP
    When: request received
    Then: connection rejected with 403 Forbidden
  [ac-4]
    Given: daemon is running
    When: any .kspec/*.yaml file changes
    Then: connected WebSocket clients receive update event via topic subscription
  [ac-5]
    Given: file watching is active
    When: rapid changes occur (< 500ms apart)
    Then: events are debounced and aggregated into single notification
  [ac-6]
    Given: watched file has YAML parse error
    When: change detected
    Then: error logged and WebSocket broadcasts error event (daemon does not crash)
  [ac-7]
    Given: .kspec directory becomes inaccessible
    When: watcher encounters error
    Then: daemon logs error and attempts recovery with exponential backoff
  [ac-8]
    Given: Bun fs.watch fails or misses events
    When: reliability issue detected
    Then: automatically fall back to Chokidar file watcher
  [ac-9]
    Given: daemon is running
    When: user runs 'kspec serve --daemon'
    Then: process detaches to background, writes PID to .kspec/.daemon.pid, CLI returns immediately
  [ac-10]
    Given: daemon is running in background
    When: user runs 'kspec serve stop'
    Then: daemon shuts down gracefully, removes PID file, closes all WebSocket connections
  [ac-11]
    Given: daemon is running
    When: GET /api/health is called
    Then: returns {status, uptime, connections, version} JSON
  [ac-12]
    Given: daemon receives SIGTERM or SIGINT
    When: shutdown signal received
    Then: graceful shutdown (flush pending messages, close connections, save state)
  [ac-13]
    Given: WebSocket connection established
    When: 30 seconds pass without activity
    Then: server sends ping frame
  [ac-14]
    Given: ping was sent
    When: no pong received within 90 seconds
    Then: connection closed with code 1001
  [ac-15]
    Given: Elysia server is configured
    When: routes are registered
    Then: use plugin pattern for middleware (CORS, logging, validation)
  [ac-16]
    Given: daemon code is ready
    When: bun build --compile runs
    Then: produces standalone executable without requiring Bun installation
  [ac-17]
    Given: daemon is running with web UI built
    When: browser opens http://localhost:<port>/
    Then: serves the built web UI assets (SvelteKit static build) as the root route

Remember: Add test coverage for each AC and mark tests with // AC: @spec-ref ac-N
